filmhouse.title: The House on the Moon
filmhouse.description: In a fantastical realm where the sun is dying, the legendary archer Ho Yi vanishes on a desperate quest to restore its light. Consumed by worry, his lover and fairy maiden Chang Er, adventures to the moon's unexplored dark side to find him. Crossing paths with an earthbound bandit whose vessel crash-lands in her domain, the mismatched pair must navigate dreamlike topographies, ancient mythologies, and their conflicting desires in a race against cosmic darkness. Directed by Nelson Yeo, this spellbinding Singaporean-Taiwanese co-production premiered in competition at Locarno Film Festival 2026. Blending folklore, surrealist imagery, and poignant intimacy, the film offers a visually poetic and hauntingly romantic reimagining of the classic Eastern mythology. *Join us on November 12 for the opening screening and an in-person Q&A with Director Nelson Yeo, and lead actress Shi-An Lim In Mandarin with English subtitles. Rated NC16 for Sexual Scene and Some Mature Content. The Way Of The Sword: Wuxia Masters is co-presented by Filmhouse and Momo Film Co, and supported by Singapore Film Society

filmhouse.title: Look Back
filmhouse.description: In a quiet town, Fujino is a confident elementary school student whose clever four-panel manga strips earn her idolization from her peers. Her artistic ego is shaken when the school paper begins publishing the astonishingly detailed artwork of Kyomoto, a reclusive classmate who refuses to leave her room. What begins as bitter jealousy transforms into a life-changing friendship when the two young creators join forces, forging an intense creative bond that carries them through the triumphs, heartbreaks, and haunting tragedies of growing into adulthood. Directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda (Shoplifters, Monster) and adapted from Tatsuki Fujimoto’s (Chainsaw Man) one-shot manga of the same name, this acclaimed live-action drama premiered at the Venice International Film Festival. Shot on tactile 35mm film, Kore-eda’s sensitive adaptation pairs nuanced performances with a deeply moving exploration of artistic creation, grief, and the quiet human connections that forever shape our lives. In Japanese with English subtitles. Rated PG for Brief Nudity.

filmhouse.title: Godzilla Minus Zero
filmhouse.description: An allegory to nuclear weapons and unchecked military power, an insanely fun kaiju spectacle, or an adorable chonky boi that just wants to vibe, you decide what Godzilla and its legendary film franchise mean to you! War reduced Japan to zero, and Godzilla plunged it into minus. Two years have passed since then, and the country has faced agonizing struggles to achieve recovery and finally reclaim its daily life. Just as humanity managed to cling to a hard-won peace, a new threat strikes, crushing hope in an instant. There is no third time. Everything ends here. In Japanese with English and Chinese subtitles. Rated PG13 for Some Violence.

filmhouse.title: Amélie (25th Anniversary)
filmhouse.description: In the bustling, hyper-saturated streets of Montmartre, shy and eccentric waitress Amélie Poulain discovers a hidden tin box of childhood treasures in her apartment. When she successfully returns it to its rightful owner, she embarks on a whimsical, clandestine crusade to orchestrate small moments of joy and justice in the lives of the colorful Parisian misfits around her. But as she plays guardian angel to others, Amélie must find the courage to pursue her own elusive romance. A globe-conquering cultural phenomenon, Jean-Pierre Jeunet’s magical realist romance remains one of the most beloved French films ever made. Powered by Audrey Tautou’s star-making performance and Yann Tiersen’s iconic accordion-laced score, Amélie is a visually intoxicating, unapologetically joyful cinematic confection that will leave you floating out of the theater. In French with English subtitles Rated M18 for Sexual Content, With the support of French Embassy, part of vOilah! French film festival

filmhouse.title: La La Land (10th Anniversary)
filmhouse.description: Mia, an aspiring actress, serves lattes to movie stars in between auditions and Sebastian, a jazz musician, scrapes by playing cocktail party gigs in dingy bars, but as success mounts they are faced with decisions that begin to fray the fragile fabric of their love affair, and the dreams they worked so hard to maintain in each other threaten to rip them apart. In English with Mandarin Subtitles Rated PG13 for Some Coarse Language

filmhouse.title: Cartoons Underground Programme C - Playground - For Kids
filmhouse.description: Cartoons Underground returns with 28 films from 17 countries across three unique programmes! Join us at Filmhouse on 14 November, 2026. New this year, Playground is our first programme made for younger audiences. These films see the world through a child's eyes with curiosity, wonder and a sense of being different. A curious child gathers experiences, a deaf child imagines the sound of a concert, and a girl sees snow differently from everyone in her art class. Made by first-time directors and student collectives, they trust young viewers to feel and wonder at once. Every film across our three official programmes is in competition. Vote for your favourite film to win the Audience Choice Award at the Golden Durian Awards. Expected G Rating. - Each programme ticket is sold individually - If you buy a ticket for 2 or more programmes, show us your proof of purchase on November 14 at Filmhouse to claim your own one-of-a-kind CU merch Presented by Cartoons Underground

filmhouse.title: Persepolis
filmhouse.description: In 1970s Iran, Marjane 'Marji' Satrapi watches events through her young eyes and her idealistic family of a long dream being fulfilled of the hated Shah's defeat in the Iranian Revolution of 1979. However as Marji grows up, she witnesses first hand how the new Iran, now ruled by Islamic fundamentalists, has become a repressive tyranny on its own. In French with English subtitles. Rated PG for Some Drug and Sexual References. With the support of French Embassy, part of vOilah! French film festival

filmhouse.title: Wildwood
filmhouse.description: When her baby brother Mac is whisked away into an impenetrable, uncharted forest by a murder of crows, young Prue and her classmate Curtis ventures on a rescue mission. They stumble into a hidden realm where talking animals, mystical creatures, and warring factions vie for control. Drawn into an impending war orchestrated by the vengeful Countess Alexandra, Prue and Curtis must navigate treacherous alliances to save Mac and preserve the fragile balance of the magical wood. Directed by Travis Knight and produced by Laika(Coraline, Kubo and the Two Strings), this epic stop-motion fantasy adapts Colin Meloy’s beloved novel into the animation studio’s most ambitious feature to date. Featuring the voices of Carey Mulligan, Mahershala Ali, and Angela Bassett, the film blends tactile, hand-crafted puppet craft with sprawling scale, offering a thrilling and breathtaking coming-of-age adventure. In English Rated PG13 for Some Violence.

filmhouse.title: Cartoons Underground Programme A - Held Breath
filmhouse.description: Cartoons Underground returns with 28 films from 17 countries across three unique programmes! Join us at Filmhouse on 14 November, 2026. Our two evening programmes pair films from around the world with works by emerging Singapore student filmmakers. Expect stop-motion, hand-drawn 2D and experimental work. Many films explore life inside our own heads: a people-pleaser faces a dark being, and a mouse dreads going outside. Others bear witness to an unstable world, including an animated diary kept through years of war. Memory, loss and mortality run through strange, tender stories like a shop owner facing his end with the help of a moth. From Singapore, young filmmakers take on the guilt of sending a dog away and a wooden doll trapped in a loop of time. They hold their own beside the international selection. Every film across our three official programmes is in competition in our International and Singapore Student Film categories. Vote for your favourite film to win the Audience Choice Award at the Golden Durian Awards. Expect NC16 Rating. - Each programme ticket is sold individually - If you buy a ticket for 2 or more programmes, show us your proof of purchase on November 14 at Filmhouse to claim your own one-of-a-kind CU merch Presented by Cartoons Underground

filmhouse.title: Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon (4K Restoration)
filmhouse.description: In 19th-century Qing Dynasty China, renowned swordsman Li Mu Bai (Chow Yun Fat) decides to retire from his life of violence, entrusting his legendary 400-year-old sword, the Green Destiny, to his unspoken love, Yu Shu Lien(Michelle Yeoh). When the blade is stolen, suspicion falls on Jen Yu(Zhang Ziyi), a rebellious young noblewoman desperate to escape an arranged marriage. As Shu Lien and Mu Bai pursue the thief across breathtaking landscapes, they uncover a web of dark secrets and hidden identities. Directed by Ang Lee, this international cinematic phenomenon made history by winning four Academy Awards, including Best Foreign Language Film. Renowned for Yuen Wo-ping’s gravity-defying action choreography and Tan Dun’s iconic cello score, the film elevates traditional wuxia into a deeply romantic, tragic, and visually staggering masterpiece of passion and restraint. In Mandarin with English subtitles. Rated NC16 for Some Intimate Scenes. The Way Of The Sword: Wuxia Masters is co-presented by Filmhouse and Momo Film Co, and supported by Singapore Film Society

Includes an intermission, Q&A with SG filmmakers, and the Golden Durian Awards Ceremony Our two evening main programmes pair films from around the world with works by emerging Singapore student filmmakers. filmhouse.title: Kokuho
filmhouse.description: Following its phenomenal success in Japan, critically acclaimed film Kokuho is enjoying a re-release in Singapore with limited screenings! Directed by acclaimed filmmaker Lee Sang-il and adapted from Shuichi Yoshida's bestselling novel of the same name, Kokuho stars Ryo Yoshizawa and Ryusei Yokohama alongside an impressive ensemble cast including Ken Watanabe. Set in the fascinating world of Kabuki, Japan's centuries-old traditional performing art, Kokuho tells the story of two young men from very different backgrounds whose lives become intertwined through their pursuit perfecting their craft. More than just a story about performance, Kokuho is a powerful portrait of ambition, identity and the price of dedicating one's life to art. Recognised by UNESCO as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, Kabuki is celebrated for its rich traditions, elaborate costumes and stylised performances. One of its most iconic features is “onnagata”, the art of male actors portraying female roles with extraordinary precision, grace and emotional depth. Since its release, Kokuho has become the highest-grossing live-action Japanese film in history. Domestic and global popularity of the film has also rekindled public interest in kabuki. The film dominated the 49th Japan Academy Film Prize, taking home ten awards, including Best Picture, Best Director and Best Actor. Its exceptional Kabuki-inspired hair and makeup artistry also earned a nomination for Best Makeup and Hairstyling at the 98th Academy Awards, bringing the beauty of Japanese traditional culture to the global stage. In Japanese with English and Mandarin dual subtitles. Rated M18 for Sexual Scenes.

filmhouse.title: Delicatessen (4K Restoration)
filmhouse.description: In a surreal, post-apocalyptic France where food is currency and times are desperately lean, an imposing landlord and butcher keeps his eclectic tenants fed with a very specialized, sinister supply of meat. When an optimistic former circus clown arrives looking for work as a handyman, he unwittingly falls for the butcher’s myopic, cello-playing daughter. To save him from the chopping block, she enlists the help of a subterranean rebel faction of vegetarian freedom fighters. A dazzling exercise in pitch-black comedy and steampunk aesthetics, Jeunet and Caro’s breakout debut is a marvel of production design and rhythmic editing. Balancing grotesque horror with Keaton-esque slapstick, this deliciously macabre cult classic remains an essential big-screen experience. In French with English subtitles Rated NC16 for Some Violence. With the support of French Embassy, part of vOilah! French film festival TW: Themes of Sexual Assault and Suicide.

filmhouse.title: Castle in the Sky
filmhouse.description: When young mining apprentice Pazu catches a girl descending gently from the heavens, he is swept into an exhilarating race across the clouds. The girl, Sheeta, carries a glowing crystal pendant coveted by ruthless military agents and a boisterous crew of air pirates. United against impossible odds, the pair take flight in search of Laputa, a mythical floating city lost inside a colossal tempest, guarding forgotten technology and perilous power. The thrilling maiden release that officially launched Studio Ghibli, Hayao Miyazaki’s steampunk epic remains a milestone of hand-drawn animation. Driven by dizzying aerial dogfights, lush world building, and Joe Hisaishi’s legendary symphonic score, Castle in the Sky is a timeless big screen spectacle of boundless wonder, heart, and pure cinematic joy. In Japanese with English subtitles. Rated G. TW: Contains scenes with flashing lights, photosensitive viewers are advised.

filmhouse.title: Fjord
filmhouse.description: The Gheorghius, a devout Romanian Norwegian couple, resettle in a village set in a distant fjord where they become close to their neighbours, the Halbergs. Their children bond despite their different education. When adolescent Elia Gheorghiu shows up at school with some bruises on her body, the community asks itself if the traditional education that the Gheorghiu children get from their parents might have anything to do with it. Winner of the Palme d’Or at the Cannes Film Festival, Fjord marks another masterclass in moral ambiguity from director Cristian Mungiu (4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days, R.M.N.). Anchored by magnetic, career-defining performances from Stan and Reinsve, the film dissects the terrifying machinery of state intervention with surgical narrative precision. Framed in stark long-take cinematography that captures the icy, claustrophobic grandeur of its Scandinavian setting, Fjord is an explosive, thought-provoking drama bound to spark debate. In Romanian and Norwegian with English subtitles. Rated NC16 for Some Nudity. TW: Contains depictions of self-harm.

filmhouse.title: The City of Lost Children (4K Restoration)
filmhouse.description: On a fog-shrouded offshore rig, the malevolent scientist Krank suffers from an inability to dream, accelerating his aging process. To stave off death, he employs a cult of cyborg cyclops to kidnap children from the nearby port city to steal their dreams. When the little brother of One, a gentle, hulking circus strongman (Ron Perlman), is abducted, One forms an unlikely alliance with a fiercely intelligent nine year old street thief to infiltrate Krank’s surreal maritime fortress. A breathtaking masterclass in world-building, The City of Lost Children pushes the visual limits of 90s practical effects and early CGI. Lensed by master cinematographer Darius Khondji, it is a haunting, Jules Verne infused gothic fairy tale that bridges the gap between dark comic book fantasy and European art cinema. In French with English subtitles. Rated NC16 for Brief Nudity. With the support of French Embassy, part of vOilah! French film festival

filmhouse.title: Mad Max: Fury Road
filmhouse.description: "Oh, what a day... what a lovely day!!" In a desolate post-apocalyptic wasteland, haunted survivor Max is captured by the War Boys, the fanatical army of the tyrannical warlord Immortan Joe. Max's fate becomes intertwined with Imperator Furiosa, a formidable captain who steals Joe's prized armored rig to smuggle the warlord’s five enslaved wives to safety. Pursued across the harsh desert by Joe's ruthless armada, Max and Furiosa forge an uneasy alliance to survive a relentless, high-octane battle on wheels. Featuring high adrenaline stunt work, kinetic editing, and a searing score, this George Miller modern classic combines muscular spectacle with an empowering narrative of survival, redemption, and liberation. Witness!! In English. Rated NC16 for Violence.

filmhouse.title: Moonlight (10th Anniversary)
filmhouse.description: Framed across three pivotal eras of his life, Chiron navigates the harsh realities of growing up in a tough neighborhood while struggling with his identity, sexuality, and a troubled home environment. Guided by the tender mentorship of a local drug dealer and a deep, enduring connection with a childhood friend, Chiron gradually leanrs to protect himself from the world as he grows into adulthood. Directed by Barry Jenkins, this groundbreaking drama won three Academy Awards, including Best Picture and Best Supporting Actor for Mahershala Ali. Celebrated for James Laxton’s luminous cinematography and Nicholas Britell’s evocative score, the film stands as a transcendent, deeply lyrical portrait of intimacy, vulnerability, and self-discovery. Newly restored in 4K and with an exclusive conversation with director Barry Jenkins, featuring Oscar Nominated composer Nicholas Britell and Oscar winner Mahershala Ali, to follow the feature. In English. Rated M18 for Some Homosexual Content.

filmhouse.title: All We Imagine as Light
filmhouse.description: In Mumbai, Prabha, a dedicated head nurse, buries her anxieties in her work while awaiting word from her estranged husband living abroad. Her younger, free-spirited roommate Anu struggles to find a private space in the bustling city to share with her secret Muslim lover. When the two women embark on a road trip to a coastal beach town alongside a retiring coworker, the change of setting offers them a space where their repressed desires, unspoken hopes, and bonds of sisterhood surfaces. Celebrated for its profound empathy, the Cannes Film Festival 2024 Grand Prix Winner offers a poetic, tender, and deeply moving portrait of female friendship, urban isolation, and the quiet search for freedom. In Malayalam, Hindi and Marathi with English subtitles . Rated M18 for Sexual Scenes.

filmhouse.title: The Blade (4K Restoration)
filmhouse.description: In a lawless and brutal country dominated by ruthless bandit clans, Ding On works as a blacksmith’s apprentice in a remote sword factory. When he discovers the truth about his father's murder, Ding On sets off on a quest for revenge after bandit leader Fei Lung. In pursuit of vengeance, Ding On narrowly escapes an ambush, but loses his right arm in the process. Finding a half-burnt martial arts manual, he strengthens his resolve, forging a broken blade and adapting his fighting style to attain his retribution. Directed by Tsui Hark, this ferocious reimagining of Chang Cheh’s 1967 wuxia classic One-Armed Swordsman is a force of visual chaos and raw aggression. Driven by wild, immersive camerawork, and a gritty atmosphere, the film remains a visceral, influential cult classic. In Cantonese with English subtitles. The Way Of The Sword: Wuxia Masters is co-presented by Filmhouse and Momo Film Co, and supported by Singapore Film Society Rated NC16 for Violence. TW: Contains depictions of animal abuse.

filmhouse.title: Look Back
filmhouse.description: In a quiet town, Fujino is a confident elementary school student whose clever four-panel manga strips earn her idolization from her peers. Her artistic ego is shaken when the school paper begins publishing the astonishingly detailed artwork of Kyomoto, a reclusive classmate who refuses to leave her room. What begins as bitter jealousy transforms into a life-changing friendship when the two young creators join forces, forging an intense creative bond that carries them through the triumphs, heartbreaks, and haunting tragedies of growing into adulthood. Directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda (Shoplifters, Monster) and adapted from Tatsuki Fujimoto’s (Chainsaw Man) one-shot manga of the same name, this acclaimed live-action drama premiered at the Venice International Film Festival. Shot on tactile 35mm film, Kore-eda’s sensitive adaptation pairs nuanced performances with a deeply moving exploration of artistic creation, grief, and the quiet human connections that forever shape our lives. In Japanese with English subtitles. Rated PG for Brief Nudity.

filmhouse.title: Kokuho
filmhouse.description: Following its phenomenal success in Japan, critically acclaimed film Kokuho is enjoying a re-release in Singapore with limited screenings! Directed by acclaimed filmmaker Lee Sang-il and adapted from Shuichi Yoshida's bestselling novel of the same name, Kokuho stars Ryo Yoshizawa and Ryusei Yokohama alongside an impressive ensemble cast including Ken Watanabe. Set in the fascinating world of Kabuki, Japan's centuries-old traditional performing art, Kokuho tells the story of two young men from very different backgrounds whose lives become intertwined through their pursuit perfecting their craft. More than just a story about performance, Kokuho is a powerful portrait of ambition, identity and the price of dedicating one's life to art. Recognised by UNESCO as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, Kabuki is celebrated for its rich traditions, elaborate costumes and stylised performances. One of its most iconic features is “onnagata”, the art of male actors portraying female roles with extraordinary precision, grace and emotional depth. Since its release, Kokuho has become the highest-grossing live-action Japanese film in history. Domestic and global popularity of the film has also rekindled public interest in kabuki. The film dominated the 49th Japan Academy Film Prize, taking home ten awards, including Best Picture, Best Director and Best Actor. Its exceptional Kabuki-inspired hair and makeup artistry also earned a nomination for Best Makeup and Hairstyling at the 98th Academy Awards, bringing the beauty of Japanese traditional culture to the global stage. In Japanese with English and Mandarin dual subtitles. Rated M18 for Sexual Scenes.

filmhouse.title: Wildwood
filmhouse.description: When her baby brother Mac is whisked away into an impenetrable, uncharted forest by a murder of crows, young Prue and her classmate Curtis ventures on a rescue mission. They stumble into a hidden realm where talking animals, mystical creatures, and warring factions vie for control. Drawn into an impending war orchestrated by the vengeful Countess Alexandra, Prue and Curtis must navigate treacherous alliances to save Mac and preserve the fragile balance of the magical wood. Directed by Travis Knight and produced by Laika(Coraline, Kubo and the Two Strings), this epic stop-motion fantasy adapts Colin Meloy’s beloved novel into the animation studio’s most ambitious feature to date. Featuring the voices of Carey Mulligan, Mahershala Ali, and Angela Bassett, the film blends tactile, hand-crafted puppet craft with sprawling scale, offering a thrilling and breathtaking coming-of-age adventure. In English Rated PG13 for Some Violence.

filmhouse.title: The House on the Moon
filmhouse.description: In a fantastical realm where the sun is dying, the legendary archer Ho Yi vanishes on a desperate quest to restore its light. Consumed by worry, his lover and fairy maiden Chang Er, adventures to the moon's unexplored dark side to find him. Crossing paths with an earthbound bandit whose vessel crash-lands in her domain, the mismatched pair must navigate dreamlike topographies, ancient mythologies, and their conflicting desires in a race against cosmic darkness. Directed by Nelson Yeo, this spellbinding Singaporean-Taiwanese co-production premiered in competition at Locarno Film Festival 2026. Blending folklore, surrealist imagery, and poignant intimacy, the film offers a visually poetic and hauntingly romantic reimagining of the classic Eastern mythology. *Join us on November 12 for the opening screening and an in-person Q&A with Director Nelson Yeo, and lead actress Shi-An Lim In Mandarin with English subtitles. Rated NC16 for Sexual Scene and Some Mature Content. The Way Of The Sword: Wuxia Masters is co-presented by Filmhouse and Momo Film Co, and supported by Singapore Film Society

filmhouse.title: Stop Making Sense (4K Restoration)
filmhouse.description: Some movies are meant to be watched in quiet contemplation; others demand to be experienced as a party. We are cranking up Filmhouse’s 7.1 sound system to present the definitive 4K restoration of Talking Heads’ cinematic milestone in all its high volume glory! Captured over three nights at Hollywood’s Pantages Theatre in 1983, Jonathan Demme’s concert film opens on an empty stage with David Byrne, an acoustic guitar, and a portable cassette player performing "Psycho Killer." Musician by musician, instrument by instrument, the stage is constructed before the audience's eyes, escalating into an exhilarating, high energy spectacle driven by Talking Heads at the peak of their live performance powers. Whether you're a lifelong fan or discovering the iconic big suit for the first time, join us for an unmissable communal screening that bridges the gap between cinema and live concert! In English. Rated PG TW: Contains scenes with flashing lights, photosensitive audiences are advised.

filmhouse.title: Castle in the Sky
filmhouse.description: When young mining apprentice Pazu catches a girl descending gently from the heavens, he is swept into an exhilarating race across the clouds. The girl, Sheeta, carries a glowing crystal pendant coveted by ruthless military agents and a boisterous crew of air pirates. United against impossible odds, the pair take flight in search of Laputa, a mythical floating city lost inside a colossal tempest, guarding forgotten technology and perilous power. The thrilling maiden release that officially launched Studio Ghibli, Hayao Miyazaki’s steampunk epic remains a milestone of hand-drawn animation. Driven by dizzying aerial dogfights, lush world building, and Joe Hisaishi’s legendary symphonic score, Castle in the Sky is a timeless big screen spectacle of boundless wonder, heart, and pure cinematic joy. In Japanese with English subtitles. Rated G. TW: Contains scenes with flashing lights, photosensitive viewers are advised.
